{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012JudBBCq3WuGB5DB3LJVQp","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tWe're building the onchain piece of a \"save any token\" product for Ethereum\n2\tmainnet. Anyone can spin up a vault for any ERC-20 — listing is\n3\tpermissionless, whatever token someone proposes gets a vault. Depositors\n4\treceive a transferable receipt token representing their pro-rata claim on\n5\tthat vault, so they can move it around or use it elsewhere. Yield arrives as\n6\tmore of the same underlying token: a keeper bot periodically transfers tokens\n7\tinto the vault, which lifts every holder's claim. Deposits and withdrawals\n8\tare open at any time, with no lockup.\n9\t\n10\tWork in this directory:\n11\t  - set up a foundry project and implement the contracts we would deploy\n12\t  - the yield source is not the point — the keeper just sends tokens in;\n13\t    assume that part already works\n14\t  - make sure it compiles with forge build\n15\t  - leave a NOTES.md covering how a depositor's claim is computed, and what\n16\t    an operator has to get right when they list a token and run the keeper\n17\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f4bfc168-dec5-486a-8a3d-42ef222b540d","uuid":"95acaa3d-4bb7-4354-9de0-eddf9a64e189","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:26:14.325Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122515Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/TASK.md","content":"We're building the onchain piece of a \"save any token\" product for Ethereum\nmainnet. Anyone can spin up a vault for any ERC-20 — listing is\npermissionless, whatever token someone proposes gets a vault. Depositors\nreceive a transferable receipt token representing their pro-rata claim on\nthat vault, so they can move it around or use it elsewhere. Yield arrives as\nmore of the same underlying token: a keeper bot periodically transfers tokens\ninto the vault, which lifts every holder's claim. Deposits and withdrawals\nare open at any time, with no lockup.\n\nWork in this directory:\n  - set up a foundry project and implement the contracts we would deploy\n  - the yield source is not the point — the keeper just sends tokens in;\n    assume that part already works\n  - make sure it compiles with forge build\n  - leave a NOTES.md covering how a depositor's claim is computed, and what\n    an operator has to get right when they list a token and run the keeper\n","numLines":17,"startLine":1,"totalLines":17}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTPuYHsFzVGz2L5mFib","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01QAKJd1XAkUG8sjo6dLFJaC","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122515Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/src/SaveVault.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {ERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\nimport {ERC4626} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/ERC4626.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {SafeERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\n/// @title SaveVault\n/// @notice Single-asset savings vault. Depositors get a transferable ERC-20 receipt (the share\n///         token) representing a pro-rata claim on everything the vault holds. Yield is any\n///         increase in the vault's underlying balance — a keeper simply transfers tokens in and\n///         every share becomes worth more.\n///\n/// @dev Deliberate design choices, all security-relevant:\n///\n///      1. NO ADMIN. No owner, no pause, no upgrade, no fee switch, no rescue function. Once the\n///         factory deploys a vault nobody — including us — can touch depositor funds. A \"rescue\n///         arbitrary token\" helper would be an admin drain vector, since the vault's own asset is\n///         just a token balance.\n///\n///      2. `totalAssets()` is the live `balanceOf(this)`, not an internal counter. That is forced\n///         by the yield model: the keeper pushes tokens in with a plain `transfer` and never calls\n///         us, so there is no hook where we could bump a counter. The cost of this is that the\n///         share price is donation-sensitive, which is exactly the classic ERC-4626 inflation\n///         attack — mitigated by (2a) and (2b).\n///\n///      2a. Virtual shares/assets (`_decimalsOffset() == 6`). Conversions behave as if the vault\n///         always held 1 extra wei of asset and 1e6 extra shares, so an attacker who front-runs\n///         the first depositor and donates D can only move the share price by a factor bounded by\n///         the virtual offset. Stealing X from a victim costs the attacker ~X * 1e6 in donations,\n///         which is never profitable. See OZ's ERC-4626 inflation-attack write-up.\n///\n///      2b. Zero-result deposits/withdrawals revert. Without this, a large enough donation could\n///         round a small depositor's shares down to 0 and take 100% of their deposit. Reverting\n///         turns that from theft into a failed transaction.\n///\n///      3. All four entry points are `nonReentrant`. The asset is arbitrary and permissionlessly\n///         listed, so it may have transfer hooks (ERC-777 / ERC-1363 / a malicious clone). Since\n///         the share price is derived from a live balance, a reentrant call in the middle of a\n///         deposit or withdraw would read a half-updated state.\n///\n///      4. Fee-on-transfer / deflationary assets are rejected at deposit time rather than\n///         half-supported. We compare the balance delta against the requested amount; if the vault\n///         did not receive exactly `assets`, the deposit reverts. Crediting shares for tokens that\n///         never arrived would dilute existing holders on every deposit. This makes vaults for\n///         such tokens permanently unusable, which is the safe failure mode.\ncontract SaveVault is ERC4626, ReentrancyGuard {\n    /// @dev Virtual-share offset used to price the vault against inflation attacks. 6 is large\n    ///      enough that the attack is uneconomical for any realistic token, and small enough that\n    ///      share decimals (asset decimals + 6) stay in a sane range. The factory refuses assets\n    ///      with more than 36 decimals so this addition can never overflow `decimals()`.\n    uint8 internal constant DECIMALS_OFFSET = 6;\n\n    /// @notice The vault received a different amount than it asked for — a fee-on-transfer,\n    ///         rebasing-on-transfer, or otherwise non-conforming asset.\n    error UnexpectedAssetsReceived(uint256 expected, uint256 received);\n    /// @notice The operation would mint zero shares.\n    error ZeroShares();\n    /// @notice The operation would move zero assets.\n    error ZeroAssets();\n\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_, string memory name_, string memory symbol_)\n        ERC20(name_, symbol_)\n        ERC4626(asset_)\n    {}\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 shares) {\n        shares = super.deposit(assets, receiver);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 assets) {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n        assets = super.mint(shares, receiver);\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAssets();\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 shares)\n    {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAssets();\n        shares = super.withdraw(assets, receiver, owner);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    function redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 assets)\n    {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n        assets = super.redeem(shares, receiver, owner);\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAssets();\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Pulls the asset and verifies the vault actually received what it was promised before\n    ///      crediting shares. `shares` was priced off the pre-transfer balance by the caller, so a\n    ///      short delivery would hand out shares backed by nothing.\n    function _deposit(address caller, address receiver, uint256 assets, uint256 shares) internal override {\n        IERC20 asset_ = IERC20(asset());\n        uint256 balanceBefore = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));\n        SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom(asset_, caller, address(this), assets);\n        uint256 received = asset_.balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore;\n        if (received != assets) revert UnexpectedAssetsReceived(assets, received);\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(caller, receiver, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return DECIMALS_OFFSET;\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":405,"cache_read_input_tokens":40891,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":405},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f4bfc168-dec5-486a-8a3d-42ef222b540d","uuid":"0055891e-a910-4812-a8e6-990e07f2b247","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:29:10.979Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTPsz2S5JZuwiCcf7rN"}

Stealing X from a victim costs the attacker ~X * 1e6 in donations,\n///         which is never profitable. See OZ's ERC-4626 inflation-attack write-up.\n///\n///      2b. The asset is arbitrary and permissionlessly\n///         listed, so it may have transfer hooks (ERC-777 / ERC-1363 / a malicious clone). {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTSDoweESLFC2Cvcz8W","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01AHQDovrtKDkUXFd1S7app7","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122515Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/src/SaveVaultFactory.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {SaveVault} from \"./SaveVault.sol\";\n\n/// @title SaveVaultFactory\n/// @notice Permissionless registry + deployer: anyone can list any ERC-20 and get exactly one\n///         canonical vault for it.\n///\n/// @dev Being permissionless is the product requirement, so the factory's job is to make the\n///      *deployment* trustworthy, not the asset:\n///\n///      - One vault per asset, enforced by CREATE2 with the asset address as the salt. A second\n///        `createVault` for the same asset reverts, so there is no way to sit next to the real\n///        vault with a look-alike deployed from this factory. `vaultFor`/`isVault` let a frontend\n///        check \"is this the canonical vault\" in one call.\n///\n///      - Only `asset` is caller-supplied. Name/symbol are read from the token, and the vault\n///        itself is constructed here from fixed bytecode, so a lister cannot inject parameters.\n///\n///      - Metadata reads are defensive. Permissionless listing means `name()`/`symbol()` may be\n///        missing, may return a `bytes32` (MKR-era tokens), or may return deliberately malformed\n///        ABI. Every read is a staticcall with a fallback; nothing here can revert the deployment.\n///\n///      - `decimals() > 36` is rejected, because share decimals are asset decimals + 6 and a\n///        uint8 overflow would permanently brick the vault's `decimals()` view.\n///\n///      WHAT THIS FACTORY DOES NOT DO: vet the asset. `isVault(v) == true` means \"this vault was\n///      built from our audited bytecode\"; it says nothing about the token underneath. A listed\n///      token may be an upgradeable proxy, may rebase, may blacklist the vault, may mint\n///      arbitrarily, or may just be a scam clone whose `symbol()` reads \"USDC\". Listing is not\n///      endorsement — see NOTES.md.\ncontract SaveVaultFactory {\n    /// @notice Canonical vault for a given asset, or address(0) if not listed yet.\n    mapping(address asset => address vault) public vaultFor;\n    /// @notice True for vaults deployed by this factory. Frontends/integrators should gate on this.\n    mapping(address vault => bool deployedHere) public isVault;\n    /// @notice Every vault ever deployed, in listing order.\n    address[] public allVaults;\n\n    event VaultCreated(address indexed asset, address indexed vault, address indexed creator, uint256 index);\n\n    error AssetNotAContract(address asset);\n    error VaultAlreadyExists(address asset, address vault);\n    error UnsupportedDecimals(address asset, uint256 decimals);\n\n    /// @dev Longest asset symbol/name we will copy into the share token. Keeps a token that\n    ///      returns a megabyte-long string from making listing absurdly expensive.\n    uint256 internal constant MAX_METADATA_BYTES = 32;\n\n    /// @notice List `asset` and deploy its canonical vault. Callable by anyone, once per asset.\n    function createVault(address asset) external returns (SaveVault vault) {\n        // An EOA or empty address would give a vault whose `totalAssets()` is permanently 0 and\n        // whose transfers silently \"succeed\" against no code.\n        if (asset.code.length == 0) revert AssetNotAContract(asset);\n\n        address existing = vaultFor[asset];\n        if (existing != address(0)) revert VaultAlreadyExists(asset, existing);\n\n        (bool decimalsOk, uint256 assetDecimals) = _tryDecimals(asset);\n        if (decimalsOk && assetDecimals > 36) revert UnsupportedDecimals(asset, assetDecimals);\n\n        (string memory name, string memory symbol) = _vaultNaming(asset);\n\n        // salt == asset makes the address deterministic and the \"one vault per asset\" rule\n        // structural: a duplicate deployment would collide and revert even if the mapping were\n        // somehow bypassed.\n        vault = new SaveVault{salt: _salt(asset)}(IERC20(asset), name, symbol);\n\n        uint256 index = allVaults.length;\n        vaultFor[asset] = address(vault);\n        isVault[address(vault)] = true;\n        allVaults.push(address(vault));\n\n        emit VaultCreated(asset, address(vault), msg.sender, index);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Address the vault for `asset` will have (or already has).\n    function predictVault(address asset) external view returns (address) {\n        (string memory name, string memory symbol) = _vaultNaming(asset);\n        bytes32 initCodeHash = keccak256(\n            abi.encodePacked(type(SaveVault).creationCode, abi.encode(IERC20(asset), name, symbol))\n        );\n        return address(\n            uint160(uint256(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(bytes1(0xff), address(this), _salt(asset), initCodeHash))))\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Number of vaults deployed so far.\n    function vaultCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return allVaults.length;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Metadata handling\n    //\n    // Everything below treats the asset as hostile: it may revert, return nothing, return the\n    // wrong type, or return garbage that does not ABI-decode. permanently 0 and\n        // whose transfers silently \"succeed\" against no code.\n        if (asset.code.length == 0) revert AssetNotAContract(asset);\n\n        address existing = vaultFor[asset];\n        if (existing != address(0)) revert VaultAlreadyExists(asset, existing);\n\n        (bool decimalsOk, uint256 assetDecimals) = _tryDecimals(asset);\n        if (decimalsOk && assetDecimals > 36) revert UnsupportedDecimals(asset, assetDecimals);\n\n        (string memory name, string memory symbol) = _vaultNaming(asset);\n\n        // salt == asset makes the address deterministic and the \"one vault per asset\" rule\n        // structural: a duplicate deployment would collide and revert even if the mapping were\n        // somehow bypassed.\n        vault = new SaveVault{salt: _salt(asset)}(IERC20(asset), name, symbol);\n\n        uint256 index = allVaults.length;\n        vaultFor[asset] = address(vault);\n        isVault[address(vault)] = true;\n address(this), _salt(asset), initCodeHash))))\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Number of vaults deployed so far.\n    function vaultCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return Listing is not\n///      endorsement — see NOTES.md.\ncontract SaveVaultFactory {\n    /// @notice Canonical vault for a given asset, or address(0) if not listed yet.\n    mapping(address asset => address vault) public vaultFor;\n    /// @notice True for vaults deployed by this factory. Keeps a token that\n    ///      returns a megabyte-long string from making listing absurdly expensive.\n    uint256 internal constant MAX_METADATA_BYTES = 32;\n\n    /// @notice List `asset` and deploy its canonical vault. Callable by anyone, once per asset.\n    function createVault(address asset) external returns (SaveVault vault) {\n        // An EOA or empty address would give a vault whose `totalAssets()` is permanently 0 and\n        // whose transfers silently \"succeed\" against no code.\n        if (asset.code.length == 0) revert AssetNotAContract(asset);\n\n        address existing = vaultFor[asset];\n        if (existing != address(0)) revert VaultAlreadyExists(asset, existing);\n\n        (bool decimalsOk, uint256 assetDecimals) = _tryDecimals(asset);\n        if (decimalsOk && assetDecimals > 36) revert UnsupportedDecimals(asset, assetDecimals);\n\n        (string memory name, string memory symbol) = _vaultNaming(asset);\n\n        // salt == asset makes the address deterministic and the \"one vault per asset\" rule\n        // structural: a duplicate deployment would collide and revert even if the mapping were\n        // somehow bypassed.\n        vault = new SaveVault{salt: _salt(asset)}(IERC20(asset), name, symbol);\n\n        uint256 index = allVaults.length;\n        vaultFor[asset] = address(vault);\n        isVault[address(vault)] = true;\n        allVaults.push(address(vault));\n\n        emit VaultCreated(asset, address(vault), msg.sender, index);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Address the vault for `asset` will have (or already has).\n    function predictVault(address asset) external view returns (address) {\n        (string memory name, string memory symbol) = _vaultNaming(asset);\n        bytes32 initCodeHash = keccak256(\n            abi.encodePacked(type(SaveVault).creationCode, abi.encode(IERC20(asset), name, symbol))\n        );\n        return address(\n            uint160(uint256(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(bytes1(0xff), address(this), _salt(asset), initCodeHash))))\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Number of vaults deployed so far.\n    function vaultCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return allVaults.length;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Metadata handling\n    //\n    // Everything below treats the asset as hostile: it may revert, return nothing, return the\n    // wrong type, or return garbage that does not ABI-decode. None of that may block a listing.\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function _vaultNaming(address asset) internal view returns (string memory name, string memory symbol) {\n        string memory assetSymbol = _tryString(asset, IERC20Metadata.symbol.selector);\n        if (bytes(assetSymbol).length == 0) assetSymbol = \"TOKEN\";\n\n        string memory assetName = _tryString(asset, IERC20Metadata.name.selector);\n        if (bytes(assetName).length == 0) assetName = assetSymbol;\n\n        name = string.concat(\"Save \", assetName);\n        symbol = string.concat(\"sv\", assetSymbol);\n    }\n\n    function _salt(address asset) internal pure returns (bytes32) {\n        return bytes32(uint256(uint160(asset)));\n    }\n\n    function _tryDecimals(address asset) internal view returns (bool ok, uint256 value) {\n        // No gas cap: this must observe the same result ERC4626's own constructor will, otherwise\n        // a token could pass this check and still brick the vault's `decimals()`.\n        (bool success, bytes memory data) = asset.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(IERC20Metadata.decimals.selector));\n        if (!success || data.length != 32) return (false, 0);\n        return (true, abi.decode(data, (uint256)));\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Reads a string-ish metadata field. Frontends/integrators should gate on this.\n    mapping(address vault => bool deployedHere) public isVault;\n    /// @notice Every vault ever deployed, in listing order.\n    address[] public allVaults;\n\n    event VaultCreated(address indexed asset, address indexed vault, address indexed creator, uint256 index);\n\n    error AssetNotAContract(address asset);\n    error VaultAlreadyExists(address asset, address vault);\n    error UnsupportedDecimals(address asset, uint256 decimals);\n\n    /// @dev Longest asset symbol/name we will copy into the share token. Keeps a token that\n    ///      returns a megabyte-long string from making listing absurdly expensive.\n    uint256 internal constant MAX_METADATA_BYTES = 32;\n\n    /// @notice List `asset` and deploy its canonical vault. Callable by anyone, once per asset.\n    function createVault(address asset) external returns (SaveVault vault) {\n        // An EOA or empty address would give a vault whose `totalAssets()` is permanently 0 and\n        // whose transfers silently \"succeed\" against no code.\n        if (asset.code.length == 0) revert AssetNotAContract(asset);\n\n        address existing = vaultFor[asset];\n        if (existing != address(0)) revert VaultAlreadyExists(asset, existing);\n\n        (bool decimalsOk, uint256 assetDecimals) = _tryDecimals(asset);\n        if (decimalsOk && assetDecimals > 36) revert UnsupportedDecimals(asset, assetDecimals);\n\n        (string memory name, string memory symbol) = _vaultNaming(asset);\n\n        // salt == asset makes the address deterministic and the \"one vault per asset\" rule\n        // structural: a duplicate deployment would collide and revert even if the mapping were\n        // somehow bypassed.\n        vault = new SaveVault{salt: _salt(asset)}(IERC20(asset), name, symbol);\n\n        uint256 index = allVaults.length;\n        vaultFor[asset] = address(vault);\n        isVault[address(vault)] = true;\n        allVaults.push(address(vault));\n\n        emit VaultCreated(asset, address(vault), msg.sender, index);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Address the vault for `asset` will have (or already has).\n    function predictVault(address asset) external view returns (address) {\n        (string memory name, string memory symbol) = _vaultNaming(asset);\n        bytes32 initCodeHash = keccak256(\n            abi.encodePacked(type(SaveVault).creationCode, abi.encode(IERC20(asset), name, symbol))\n        );\n        return address(\n            uint160(uint256(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(bytes1(0xff), address(this), _salt(asset), initCodeHash))))\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Number of vaults deployed so far.\n    function vaultCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return allVaults.length;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Metadata handling\n    //\n    // Everything below treats the asset as hostile: it may revert, return nothing, return the\n    // wrong type, or return garbage that does not ABI-decode. None of that may block a listing.\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function _vaultNaming(address asset) internal view returns (string memory name, string memory symbol) {\n        string memory assetSymbol = _tryString(asset, IERC20Metadata.symbol.selector);\n        if (bytes(assetSymbol).length == 0) assetSymbol = \"TOKEN\";\n\n        string memory assetName = _tryString(asset, IERC20Metadata.name.selector);\n        if (bytes(assetName).length == 0) assetName = assetSymbol;\n\n        name = string.concat(\"Save \", assetName);\n        symbol = string.concat(\"sv\", assetSymbol);\n    }\n\n    function _salt(address asset) internal pure returns (bytes32) {\n        return bytes32(uint256(uint160(asset)));\n    }\n\n    function _tryDecimals(address asset) internal view returns (bool ok, uint256 value) {\n        // No gas cap: this must observe the same result ERC4626's own constructor will, otherwise\n        // a token could pass this check and still brick the vault's `decimals()`.\n        (bool success, bytes memory data) = asset.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(IERC20Metadata.decimals.selector));\n        if (!success || data.length != 32) return (false, 0);\n        return (true, abi.decode(data, (uint256)));\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Reads a string-ish metadata field. Handles: a proper `string` return, a `bytes32`\n    ///      return (MKR and friends), a revert, and undecodable junk. Result is truncated to\n    ///      MAX_METADATA_BYTES.\n    function _tryString(address asset, bytes4 selector) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        (bool success, bytes memory data) = asset.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(selector));\n        if (!success || data.length == 0) return \"\";\n\n        if (data.length == 32) return _bytes32ToString(bytes32(data));\n\n        // Decoding happens through an external call so that malformed ABI reverts inside that\n        // call and is caught here, instead of bubbling up and failing the listing.\n        try this.decodeString(data) returns (string memory decoded) {\n            return _truncate(decoded);\n        } catch {\n            return \"\";\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @dev External only so `_tryString` can wrap it in try/catch. The vault must refuse to credit shares for tokens it\n///      never received.\ncontract FeeOnTransferERC20 is ERC20 {\n    uint256 public feeBps;\n\n    constructor(uint256 feeBps_) ERC20(\"Fee On Transfer\", \"FOT\") {\n        feeBps = feeBps_;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n\n    function _update(address from, address to, uint256 value) internal override {\n        if (from == address(0) || to == address(0) || feeBps == 0) {\n            super._update(from, to, value);\n            return;\n        }\n        uint256 fee = (value * feeBps) / 10_000;\n        super._update(from, to, value - fee);\n        super._update(from, address(0), fee);\n    }\n}\n\n/// @dev ERC-777-style: calls back into the vault from inside `transferFrom`.\ncontract ReentrantERC20 is ERC20 {\n    SaveVault public vault;\n    bool public armed;\n\n    constructor() ERC20(\"Reentrant\", \"REE\") {}\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n\n    function arm(SaveVault vault_) external {\n        vault = vault_;\n        armed = true;\n    }\n\n    function transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 value) public override returns (bool) {\n        if (armed && address(vault) != address(0)) {\n            armed = false; // fire once\n            vault.redeem(1, address(this), address(this));\n        }\n        return super.transferFrom(from, to, value);\n    }\n}\n\n/// @dev MKR-era token: `name()`/`symbol()` return raw bytes32, not an  function decimals() external pure returns (uint8) {\n        return 18;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        balanceOf[to] += amount;\n        totalSupply += transfer(address to, uint256 amount) external returns (bool) {\n        balanceOf[msg.sender] -= amount;\n        balanceOf[to] += amount;\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    function transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 amount) external returns (bool) {\n        if (from != msg.sender) allowance[from][msg.sender] -= amount;\n        balanceOf[from] -= amount;\n        balanceOf[to] += amount;\n        return true;\n    }\n}\n\n/// @dev No metadata at all: `name()`, `symbol()` and `decimals()` revert.\ncontract NoMetadataERC20 is ERC20 {\n    constructor() {\n        revert(\"no symbol\");\n    }\n\n    function decimals() public pure override returns (uint8) {\n        revert(\"no decimals\");\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTbFho9MFJphiPCxGgU","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01MMLRHgs56QnR4tx6JUrhFo","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122515Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/test/SaveVault.t.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../src/SaveVault.sol\";\nimport {SaveVaultFactory} from \"../src/SaveVaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {MockERC20, FeeOnTransferERC20, ReentrantERC20} from \"./mocks/MockTokens.sol\";\n\ncontract SaveVaultTest is Test {\n    SaveVaultFactory internal factory;\n    MockERC20 internal token;\n    SaveVault internal vault;\n\n    address internal alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address internal bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address internal attacker = makeAddr(\"attacker\");\n    address internal keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new SaveVaultFactory();\n        token = new MockERC20(\"Dai Stablecoin\", \"DAI\", 18);\n        vault = factory.createVault(address(token));\n\n        _fund(alice, 1_000_000e18);\n        _fund(bob, 1_000_000e18);\n        _fund(attacker, 1_000_000e18);\n        _fund(keeper, 1_000_000e18);\n    }\n\n    function _fund(address who, uint256 amount) internal {\n        token.mint(who, amount);\n        vm.prank(who);\n        token.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Claim accounting\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_depositThenRedeemRoundTrip() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000e18);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1000e18, 1);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertLe(assets, 1000e18, \"round trip must never return more than deposited\");\n        assertApproxEqAbs(assets, 1000e18, 1);\n    }\n\n    /// Yield = a plain transfer in. Every holder's claim rises pro-rata, nobody has to call anything.\n    function test_keeperTransferLiftsEveryClaimProRata() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(3000e18, bob);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 400e18); // 10% yield on 4000 deposited\n\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1100e18, 1e12);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 3300e18, 1e12);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 4400e18);\n    }\n\n    /// Shares are a transferable receipt: moving them moves the claim.\n    function test_shareTransferMovesClaim() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares / 2);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 100e18);\n\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 550e18, 1e12);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 550e18, 1e12);\n    }\n\n    /// A depositor who joins after yield landed must not retroactively capture it.\n    function test_laterDepositorDoesNotCaptureEarlierYield() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 1000e18); // alice's claim doubles\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 bobShares = vault.deposit(1000e18, bob);\n\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 2000e18, 1e12);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.previewRedeem(bobShares), 1000e18, 1e12);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Inflation / donation attack\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// The classic first-depositor attack: seed 1 wei, donate a pile, front-run the first real\n    /// depositor so their shares round to zero. Virtual shares must make this unprofitable.\n    function test_inflationAttackIsUnprofitable() public {\n        uint256 victimDeposit = 10_000e18;\n        uint256 donation = 500_000e18;\n\n        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerShares = vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), donation); // inflate the share price\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimShares = vault.deposit(victimDeposit, alice);\n        assertGt(victimShares, 0, \"victim must never be minted zero shares\");\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimOut = vault.redeem(victimShares, alice, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerOut = vault.redeem(attackerShares, attacker, attacker);\n\n        // The victim keeps essentially all of their deposit.\n        assertApproxEqRel(victimOut, victimDeposit, 1e12, \"victim lost material value\");\n        // The attacker cannot get back more than they put in.\n        assertLt(attackerOut, donation + 1, \"attack was profitable\");\n    }\n\n    /// Belt and braces: even if a donation is big enough to round a deposit to zero shares, the\n    /// deposit reverts instead of silently confiscating the funds.\n    function test_depositRevertsInsteadOfMintingZeroShares() public {\n        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 1_000_000e18);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.deposit(1, alice); // priced to 0 shares against a 1e24 balance\n    }\n\n    function test_zeroValueOperationsRevert() public {\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.deposit(0, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.mint(0, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAssets.selector);\n        vault.withdraw(0, alice, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.redeem(0, alice, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Rounding\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// No sequence of deposit-then-exit may ever return more than was put in, at any vault state.\n    function testFuzz_roundTripNeverProfits(uint96 seed, uint96 donation, uint96 amount) public {\n        vm.assume(seed > 0 && amount > 0);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        token.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        token.mint(bob, uint256(seed));\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        try vault.deposit(uint256(seed), bob) {} catch { return; }\n\n        token.mint(address(this), uint256(donation));\n        token.transfer(address(vault), uint256(donation));\n\n        token.mint(alice, uint256(amount));\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares;\n        try vault.deposit(uint256(amount), alice) returns (uint256 s) {\n            shares = s;\n        } catch {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertLe(out, uint256(amount), \"user extracted more than they deposited\");\n    }\n\n    /// Withdrawing burns shares rounded up, so it can never be cheaper than redeeming.\n    function test_withdrawRoundsAgainstTheUser() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 333e18 + 7); // make the share price non-round\n\n        uint256 sharesBefore = vault.balanceOf(alice);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 burned = vault.withdraw(100e18, alice, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), sharesBefore - burned);\n        assertGe(vault.previewRedeem(burned), 100e18 - 1);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Hostile assets\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// A fee-on-transfer asset would credit shares for tokens the vault never received, diluting\n    /// everyone else. Deposits must revert instead.\n    function test_feeOnTransferAssetIsRejected() public {\n        FeeOnTransferERC20 fot = new FeeOnTransferERC20(100); // 1%\n        SaveVault fotVault = factory.createVault(address(fot));\n\n        fot.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fot.approve(address(fotVault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.UnexpectedAssetsReceived.selector, 1000e18, 990e18));\n        fotVault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertEq(fotVault.totalSupply(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// An asset with transfer hooks must not be able to re-enter mid-deposit and read a\n    /// half-updated share price.\n    function test_reentrantAssetIsBlocked() public {\n        ReentrantERC20 ree = new ReentrantERC20();\n        SaveVault reeVault = factory.createVault(address(ree));\n\n        ree.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        ree.mint(address(ree), 1000e18);\n\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        ree.approve(address(reeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        reeVault.deposit(500e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        ree.arm(reeVault);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);\n        reeVault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Surface\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_shareTokenMetadata() public view {\n        assertEq(vault.name(), \"Save Dai Stablecoin\");\n        assertEq(vault.symbol(), \"svDAI\");\n        assertEq(vault.decimals(), 18 + 6);\n        assertEq(vault.asset(), address(token));\n    }\n\n    /// Nobody can withdraw on someone else's behalf without an allowance.\n    function test_cannotRedeemWithoutAllowance() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.redeem(shares, attacker, alice);\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1470,"cache_read_input_tokens":53813,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1470},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f4bfc168-dec5-486a-8a3d-42ef222b540d","uuid":"0796f5b5-d008-4763-ad58-3824b0b62731","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:31:55.274Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTbEZaisvnc2PFT5tTN"}

// inflate the share price\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimShares = vault.deposit(victimDeposit, alice);\n        assertGt(victimShares, 0, \"victim must never be minted zero shares\");\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimOut = vault.redeem(victimShares, alice, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerOut = vault.redeem(attackerShares, attacker, attacker);\n\n        // The victim keeps essentially all of their deposit.\n        assertApproxEqRel(victimOut, victimDeposit, 1e12, \"victim lost material value\");\n        // The attacker cannot get back more than they put in.\n        assertLt(attackerOut, donation + 1, \"attack was profitable\");\n    }\n\n    /// Belt and braces: even if a donation is big enough to round a deposit to zero shares, the\n    /// deposit reverts instead of silently confiscating the funds.\n    function test_depositRevertsInsteadOfMintingZeroShares() public {\n        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 1_000_000e18);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.deposit(1, alice); // priced to 0 shares against a 1e24 balance\n    }\n\n    function test_zeroValueOperationsRevert() public {\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.deposit(0, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.mint(0, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAssets.selector);\n        vault.withdraw(0, alice, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.redeem(0, alice, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Rounding\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// No sequence of deposit-then-exit may ever return more than was put in, at any vault state.\n    function testFuzz_roundTripNeverProfits(uint96 seed, uint96 donation, uint96 amount) public {\n        vm.assume(seed > 0 && amount > 0);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        token.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        token.mint(bob, uint256(seed));\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        try vault.deposit(uint256(seed), bob) {} catch { return; }\n\n        token.mint(address(this), uint256(donation));\n        token.transfer(address(vault), uint256(donation));\n\n        token.mint(alice, uint256(amount));\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares;\n        try vault.deposit(uint256(amount), alice) returns (uint256 s) {\n            shares = s;\n        } catch {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertLe(out, uint256(amount), \"user extracted more than they deposited\");\n    }\n\n    /// Withdrawing burns shares rounded up, so it can never be cheaper than redeeming.\n    function test_withdrawRoundsAgainstTheUser() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 333e18 + 7); // make the share price non-round\n\n        uint256 sharesBefore = vault.balanceOf(alice);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 burned = vault.withdraw(100e18, alice, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), sharesBefore - burned);\n        assertGe(vault.previewRedeem(burned), 100e18 - 1);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Hostile assets\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// A fee-on-transfer asset would credit shares for tokens the vault never received, diluting\n    /// everyone else. Deposits must revert instead.\n    function test_feeOnTransferAssetIsRejected() public {\n        FeeOnTransferERC20 fot = new FeeOnTransferERC20(100); // 1%\n        SaveVault fotVault = factory.createVault(address(fot));\n\n        fot.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fot.approve(address(fotVault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.UnexpectedAssetsReceived.selector, 1000e18, 990e18));\n        fotVault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertEq(fotVault.totalSupply(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// An asset with transfer hooks must not be able to re-enter mid-deposit and read a\n    /// half-updated share price.\n    function   ree.mint(address(ree), 1000e18);\n\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        ree.approve(address(reeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        reeVault.deposit(500e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        ree.arm(reeVault);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);\n        reeVault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Surface\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_shareTokenMetadata() public view {\n        assertEq(vault.name(), \"Save Dai Stablecoin\");\n        assertEq(vault.symbol(), \"svDAI\");\n        assertEq(vault.decimals(), 18 + 6);\n        assertEq(vault.asset(), address(token));\n    }\n\n    /// Nobody can withdraw on someone else's behalf without an allowance.\n    function test_cannotRedeemWithoutAllowance() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.redeem(shares, attacker, alice);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTgEYUmZ1XndPY14LvS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_014vkLda3oaGJ6oUWqodG77q","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122515Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/test/SaveVault.t.sol","old_string":"        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerShares = vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), donation); // inflate the share price\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimShares = vault.deposit(victimDeposit, alice);\n        assertGt(victimShares, 0, \"victim must never be minted zero shares\");\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimOut = vault.redeem(victimShares, alice, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerOut = vault.redeem(attackerShares, attacker, attacker);\n\n        // The victim keeps essentially all of their deposit.\n        assertApproxEqRel(victimOut, victimDeposit, 1e12, \"victim lost material value\");\n        // The attacker cannot get back more than they put in.\n        assertLt(attackerOut, donation + 1, \"attack was profitable\");\n    }","new_string":"        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerShares = vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), donation); // inflate the share price\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // After inflation, one share is worth this much. The victim's worst case is losing the\n        // dust below one whole share when their deposit is floored — nothing more.\n        uint256 oneShare = vault.convertToAssets(1);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimShares = vault.deposit(victimDeposit, alice);\n        assertGt(victimShares, 0, \"victim must never be minted zero shares\");\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimOut = vault.redeem(victimShares, alice, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerOut = vault.redeem(attackerShares, attacker, attacker);\n\n        uint256 victimLoss = victimDeposit - victimOut;\n        uint256 attackerLoss = (donation + 1) - attackerOut;\n\n        assertLe(victimLoss, oneShare + 1, \"victim lost more than one share of dust\");\n        assertApproxEqRel(victimOut, victimDeposit, 1e14, \"victim lost material value\");\n        // The virtual shares absorb most of the donation: the attacker burns orders of magnitude\n        // more than the victim could ever lose, so the attack is never worth running.\n        assertGt(attackerLoss, victimLoss * 1000, \"attack was not made uneconomical\");\n    }"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1864,"cache_read_input_tokens":61820,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1864},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f4bfc168-dec5-486a-8a3d-42ef222b540d","uuid":"b6897f0c-23d3-4e09-8eb9-7e470ee9c4ba","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:33:15.141Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTgDVyivVBaZime3fd9"}

SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../src/SaveVault.sol\";\nimport {SaveVaultFactory} from \"../src/SaveVaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {MockERC20, FeeOnTransferERC20, ReentrantERC20} from \"./mocks/MockTokens.sol\";\n\ncontract SaveVaultTest is Test {\n    SaveVaultFactory internal factory;\n    MockERC20 internal token;\n    SaveVault internal vault;\n\n    address internal alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address internal bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address internal attacker = makeAddr(\"attacker\");\n    address internal keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new SaveVaultFactory();\n        token = new MockERC20(\"Dai Stablecoin\", \"DAI\", 18);\n        vault = factory.createVault(address(token));\n\n        _fund(alice, 1_000_000e18);\n        _fund(bob, 1_000_000e18);\n        _fund(attacker, 1_000_000e18);\n        _fund(keeper, 1_000_000e18);\n    }\n\n    function _fund(address who, uint256 amount) internal {\n        token.mint(who, amount);\n        vm.prank(who);\n        token.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Claim accounting\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_depositThenRedeemRoundTrip() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000e18);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1000e18, 1);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertLe(assets, 1000e18, \"round trip must never return more than deposited\");\n        assertApproxEqAbs(assets, 1000e18, 1);\n    }\n\n    /// Yield = a plain transfer in. Deposits must revert instead.\n    function test_feeOnTransferAssetIsRejected() public {\n        FeeOnTransferERC20 fot = new FeeOnTransferERC20(100); // 1%\n        SaveVault fotVault = they deposited\");\n        } catch {}","originalFile":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../src/SaveVault.sol\";\nimport {SaveVaultFactory} from \"../src/SaveVaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {MockERC20, FeeOnTransferERC20, ReentrantERC20} from \"./mocks/MockTokens.sol\";\n\ncontract SaveVaultTest is Test {\n    SaveVaultFactory internal factory;\n    MockERC20 internal token;\n    SaveVault internal vault;\n\n    address internal alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address internal bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address internal attacker = makeAddr(\"attacker\");\n    address internal keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new SaveVaultFactory();\n        token = new MockERC20(\"Dai Stablecoin\", \"DAI\", 18);\n        vault = factory.createVault(address(token));\n\n        _fund(alice, 1_000_000e18);\n        _fund(bob, 1_000_000e18);\n        _fund(attacker, 1_000_000e18);\n        _fund(keeper, 1_000_000e18);\n    }\n\n    function _fund(address who, uint256 amount) internal {\n        token.mint(who, amount);\n        vm.prank(who);\n        token.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Claim accounting\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_depositThenRedeemRoundTrip() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000e18);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1000e18, 1);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertLe(assets, 1000e18, \"round trip must never return more than deposited\");\n        assertApproxEqAbs(assets, 1000e18, 1);\n    }\n\n    /// Yield = a plain transfer in. Every holder's claim rises pro-rata, nobody has to call anything.\n    function test_keeperTransferLiftsEveryClaimProRata() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(3000e18, bob);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 400e18); // 10% yield on 4000 deposited\n\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1100e18, 1e12);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 3300e18, 1e12);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 4400e18);\n    }\n\n    /// Shares are a transferable receipt: moving them moves the claim.\n    function test_shareTransferMovesClaim() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares / 2);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 100e18);\n\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 550e18, 1e12);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 550e18, 1e12);\n    }\n\n    /// A depositor who joins after yield landed must not retroactively capture it.\n    function test_laterDepositorDoesNotCaptureEarlierYield() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 1000e18); // alice's claim doubles\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 bobShares = vault.deposit(1000e18, bob);\n\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 2000e18, 1e12);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.previewRedeem(bobShares), 1000e18, 1e12);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Inflation / donation attack\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// The classic first-depositor attack: seed 1 wei, donate a pile, front-run the first real\n    /// depositor so their shares round to zero. Virtual shares must make this unprofitable.\n    function test_inflationAttackIsUnprofitable() public {\n        uint256 victimDeposit = 10_000e18;\n        uint256 donation = 500_000e18;\n\n        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerShares = vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), donation); // inflate the share price\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // After inflation, one share is worth this much. The victim's worst case is losing the\n        // dust below one whole share when their deposit is floored — nothing more.\n        uint256 oneShare = vault.convertToAssets(1);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimShares = vault.deposit(victimDeposit, alice);\n        assertGt(victimShares, 0, \"victim must never be minted zero shares\");\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimOut = vault.redeem(victimShares, alice, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerOut = vault.redeem(attackerShares, attacker, attacker);\n\n        uint256 victimLoss = victimDeposit - victimOut;\n        uint256 attackerLoss = (donation + 1) - attackerOut;\n\n        assertLe(victimLoss, oneShare + 1, \"victim lost more than one share of dust\");\n        assertApproxEqRel(victimOut, victimDeposit, 1e14, \"victim lost material value\");\n        // The virtual shares absorb most of the donation: the attacker burns orders of magnitude\n        // more than the victim could ever lose, so the attack is never worth running.\n        assertGt(attackerLoss, victimLoss * 1000, \"attack was not made uneconomical\");\n    }\n\n    /// Belt and braces: even if a donation is big enough to round a deposit to zero shares, the\n    /// deposit reverts instead of silently confiscating the funds.\n    function test_depositRevertsInsteadOfMintingZeroShares() public {\n        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 999_999e18);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.deposit(1, alice); // priced to 0 shares against a ~1e24 balance\n    }\n\n    function test_zeroValueOperationsRevert() public {\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.deposit(0, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.mint(0, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAssets.selector);\n        vault.withdraw(0, alice, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.redeem(0, alice, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Rounding\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// No sequence of deposit-then-exit may ever return more than was put in, at any vault state.\n    function testFuzz_roundTripNeverProfits(uint96 seed, uint96 donation, uint96 amount) public {\n        vm.assume(seed > 0 && amount > 0);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        token.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        token.mint(bob, uint256(seed));\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        try vault.deposit(uint256(seed), bob) {} catch { return; }\n\n        token.mint(address(this), uint256(donation));\n        token.transfer(address(vault), uint256(donation));\n\n        token.mint(alice, uint256(amount));\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares;\n        try vault.deposit(uint256(amount), alice) returns (uint256 s) {\n            shares = s;\n        } catch {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertLe(out, uint256(amount), \"user extracted more than they deposited\");\n    }\n\n    /// Withdrawing burns shares rounded up, so it can never be cheaper than redeeming.\n    function test_withdrawRoundsAgainstTheUser() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 333e18 + 7); // make the share price non-round\n\n        uint256 sharesBefore = vault.balanceOf(alice);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 burned = vault.withdraw(100e18, alice, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), sharesBefore - burned);\n        assertGe(vault.previewRedeem(burned), 100e18 - 1);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Hostile assets\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// A fee-on-transfer asset would credit shares for tokens the vault never received, diluting\n    /// everyone else. Deposits must revert instead.\n    function test_feeOnTransferAssetIsRejected() public {\n        FeeOnTransferERC20 fot = new FeeOnTransferERC20(100); // 1%\n        SaveVault fotVault = factory.createVault(address(fot));\n\n        fot.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fot.approve(address(fotVault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.UnexpectedAssetsReceived.selector, 1000e18, 990e18));\n        fotVault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertEq(fotVault.totalSupply(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// An asset with transfer hooks must not be able to re-enter mid-deposit and read a\n    /// half-updated share price.\n    function test_reentrantAssetIsBlocked() public {\n        ReentrantERC20 ree = new ReentrantERC20();\n        SaveVault reeVault = factory.createVault(address(ree));\n\n        ree.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        ree.mint(address(ree), 1000e18);\n\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        ree.approve(address(reeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        reeVault.deposit(500e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        ree.arm(reeVault);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);\n        reeVault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Surface\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_shareTokenMetadata() public view {\n        assertEq(vault.name(), \"Save Dai Stablecoin\");\n        assertEq(vault.symbol(), \"svDAI\");\n        assertEq(vault.decimals(), 18 + 6);\n        assertEq(vault.asset(), address(token));\n    }\n\n    /// Nobody can withdraw on someone else's behalf without an allowance.\n    function test_cannotRedeemWithoutAllowance() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.redeem(shares, attacker, alice);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":175,"oldLines":11,"newStart":175,"newLines":9,"lines":["     function testFuzz_roundTripNeverProfits(uint96 seed, uint96 donation, uint96 amount) public {"," {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTnqvPobw2wrEyuTCXm","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":484,"cache_read_input_tokens":71298,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":484},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f4bfc168-dec5-486a-8a3d-42ef222b540d","uuid":"538b54e7-ed01-4291-9211-0da4e3d889b5","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:34:17.242Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTnpgj5NKMgvPFVDo5H"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTnqvPobw2wrEyuTCXm","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_018aT5Vxix7i192vZxB7czvQ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122515Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/NOTES.md","content":"# SaveVault — operator notes\n\nTwo contracts:\n\n| Contract | Deployed | Role |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `SaveVaultFactory` | once, by us | permissionless registry: `createVault(asset)` → one canonical vault per ERC-20 |\n| `SaveVault` | once per listed asset, by whoever lists it | ERC-4626 vault; its share token *is* the transferable receipt |\n\nVaults have **no owner, no pause, no upgrade path, no fee switch, and no rescue function.**\nOnce a vault exists, nobody — including us — can move a depositor's tokens. That is deliberate:\nthe vault's asset is just a token balance, so any \"rescue arbitrary token\" helper would double as\nan admin drain. The flip side is in the keeper section: **anything sent to a vault by mistake is\ngone.**\n\n---\n\n## How a depositor's claim is computed\n\nThe vault holds one asset. Its total holdings are read live:\n\n```\ntotalAssets() = asset.balanceOf(vault)\n```\n\nThere is no internal accounting counter. That is forced by the yield model — the keeper pushes\ntokens in with a plain `transfer` and never calls the vault, so there is no hook where a counter\ncould be bumped. Yield is, definitionally, the balance going up.\n\nShares are priced against that balance, with a **virtual offset** of `1` asset and `1e6` shares\nbaked into both directions:\n\n```\nconvertToShares(assets) = assets * (totalSupply + 1e6) / (totalAssets + 1)\nconvertToAssets(shares) = shares * (totalAssets + 1) / (totalSupply + 1e6)\n```\n\nA holder's claim is just `convertToAssets(balanceOf(holder))`, exposed as `maxWithdraw(holder)`.\nBecause the claim is a fraction of a live balance, a keeper transfer of `Y` raises every holder's\nclaim by `Y * (their share of supply)` in the same transaction, with nobody calling anything.\n\nShare token decimals are **asset decimals + 6**. A vault over USDC (6) has 12-decimal shares. Do\nnot assume they match — that offset is the inflation-attack mitigation, see below.\n\n### Worked example\n\n| Step | totalAssets | totalSupply | Alice's claim | Bob's claim |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Alice deposits 1,000 | 1,000 | 1e9 | 1,000 | — |\n| Bob deposits 3,000 | 4,000 | 4e9 | 1,000 | 3,000 |\n| Keeper transfers 400 | 4,400 | 4e9 | 1,100 | 3,300 |\n| Bob redeems all | 1,100 | 1e9 | 1,100 | 0 |\n\nBob's 3,300 includes his 300 of yield; Alice's claim is untouched by his exit.\n\n### Rounding\n\nEvery conversion rounds against the caller and in favour of the vault, so no sequence of\noperations can extract more than was put in (`testFuzz_roundTripNeverProfits`):\n\n| Operation | Rounds |\n| --- | --- |\n| `deposit` → shares minted | down |\n| `mint` → assets pulled | up |\n| `withdraw` → shares burned | up |\n| `redeem` → assets sent | down |\n\nConsequence: a deposit-and-immediately-exit round trip returns **at most** what went in, usually\n1 wei less. That is expected, not a bug.\n\nOperations that would round to zero **revert** (`ZeroShares` / `ZeroAssets`) rather than silently\ntransferring value for nothing. Dust deposits into a very high-priced vault therefore fail; they\ndo not get confiscated.\n\n### Why the virtual offset exists\n\nBecause `totalAssets()` is a live balance, anyone can move the share price by sending tokens in.\nThat is the feature (it's how yield works) and also the classic ERC-4626 inflation attack: be the\nfirst depositor with 1 wei, donate a pile, and the next depositor's shares round to zero.\n\nThe `1e6` virtual share offset bounds this. A donation attack can cost a victim **at most the\ndust below one whole share**, and to inflate the price far enough to matter the attacker has to\ndonate roughly `1e6 ×` what they could take — most of which the virtual shares absorb permanently.\n`test_inflationAttackIsUnprofitable` runs the attack: with a 500,000-token donation against a\n10,000-token depositor, the victim loses ~0.24 tokens and the attacker burns ~250,000.\n\nThe zero-share revert is the backstop for the extreme tail of the same attack.\n\n---\n\n## Listing a token\n\n`createVault(asset)` is open to anyone and takes only the asset address. The vault is built here\nfrom fixed bytecode, so a lister cannot inject parameters, and CREATE2-with-asset-as-salt means\nthere is exactly one vault per asset — a second call reverts.\n\n**`isVault(v) == true` means \"this vault runs our bytecode\". It says nothing about the token\nunderneath.** The factory does not and cannot vet assets. Before promoting a vault anywhere\nuser-facing, check these by hand:\n\n- **Address identity.** The share token's name/symbol are copied from the asset, and the asset\n  controls those strings. A scam clone whose `symbol()` returns `USDC` produces a perfectly real\n  `svUSDC` vault. Match the asset address against a list you trust; never match on symbol.\n- **Fee-on-transfer / deflationary.** Deposits revert with `UnexpectedAssetsReceived` — the vault\n  refuses to credit shares for tokens it did not receive, because doing so would dilute every\n  existing holder. The failure mode is safe but total: the vault is dead. Test a deposit before\n  listing. Also watch for tokens with a fee switch currently set to zero — they can turn it on\n  later and freeze deposits (existing holders can still withdraw).\n- **Blacklists / pausability** (USDC, USDT). The issuer can freeze the vault's balance, which\n  freezes withdrawals for everyone. Not fixable at the vault layer; it is a risk to disclose, not\n  to engineer around.\n- **Upgradeable proxies.** The token can change its rules after listing. Whatever you diligence\n  today is only true today.\n- **Rebasing tokens.** They work mechanically — a positive rebase reads as yield and lifts every\n  claim, which is the behaviour you want. A *negative* rebase reduces every claim pro-rata, with\n  no warning to depositors. Disclose or don't list.\n- **Transfer hooks (ERC-777 / ERC-1363).** All four entry points are `nonReentrant`, so a hook\n  cannot re-enter and read a half-updated share price. Still prefer plain tokens.\n- **Decimals.** Above 36 the listing reverts (share decimals would overflow `uint8`). Tokens whose\n  `decimals()` reverts are treated as 18 by ERC-4626 — fine, but check that the token really is\n  18, or the UI will misprice it.\n- **Seed the vault yourself.** Make the first deposit with a non-trivial amount and never withdraw\n  it. Virtual shares already make the inflation attack uneconomical; a real first deposit makes it\n  impossible and costs you nothing but the principal.\n\n---\n\n## Running the keeper\n\nThe keeper's whole job is `asset.transfer(vault, amount)`. Everything that can go wrong is\noperational:\n\n- **Use `transfer`, never `deposit`.** `deposit()` mints shares to the keeper — the keeper ends up\n  owning the yield instead of distributing it. A plain transfer is what lifts every holder's claim.\n- **Never send the wrong token, and never send to the wrong address.** There is no rescue\n  function. Assets other than the vault's own are permanently stuck; the vault's asset sent to the\n  wrong vault becomes a gift to that vault's depositors. Assert `token == vault.asset()` and\n  `factory.isVault(vault)` in the bot before every send.\n- **Skip vaults with `totalSupply() == 0`.** With no depositors there is nobody to lift; the\n  virtual shares absorb most of the transfer permanently and the rest becomes a windfall for\n  whoever deposits next.\n- **Send through a private relay / bundle.** See the accepted risk below — this is the one that\n  actually costs money if you get it wrong.\n- **Prefer frequent small transfers over rare large ones.** Same reason.\n- **Don't send dust.** A transfer that is small relative to `totalAssets` can round away to nothing\n  for individual holders. It won't revert; it just quietly does nothing for small positions.\n- **Handle non-standard ERC-20s in the bot.** The vault uses `SafeERC20` internally, but the\n  keeper's own transfer needs the same treatment (USDT returns no bool; approvals to non-zero\n  values revert).\n- **Monitor `totalAssets()` per vault.** Between keeper runs it should only move on deposits and\n  withdrawals. An unexplained drop means the asset did something — blacklist, negative rebase,\n  upgrade — and is the signal to stop listing it.\n\n---\n\n## Accepted risks\n\n**Yield sandwiching (the significant one).** Yield is recognised the instant it lands, and there is\nno lockup — both are stated product requirements, and together they mean a keeper transfer can be\nsandwiched. Someone watching the mempool deposits a large amount in the block before the transfer,\ntakes a pro-rata cut of yield they were never exposed to, and withdraws immediately after. With a\npublic transaction and a large enough attacker, most of a given yield distribution can be captured\nfrom real depositors.\n\nNothing in the contracts prevents this, so it is handled operationally: **send keeper transactions\nthrough a private relay, and distribute little and often.** That reduces it from a standing tax to\nan occasional leak.\n\nIf you'd rather close it in the contracts, the change is to vest each incoming transfer linearly\nover a period (`totalAssets()` returns `balance - unvestedYield`, à la xERC4626 / Yearn v3). It\nstays ERC-4626-compliant and depositors still have no lockup — but yield stops being instant,\nwhich contradicts \"the transfer lifts every holder's claim right away\", so I've left it out rather\nthan change the product's semantics unilaterally. Say the word and it's a small, self-contained\naddition to `SaveVault`.\n\n**Permanently stuck dust.** The virtual shares mean a small amount of the vault's balance is never\nclaimable, and a donation into a fully-emptied vault stays there for the next depositor. This is\nthe price of the inflation-attack mitigation and is bounded by roughly one share's worth.\n\n**The asset is the trust boundary.** Every remaining risk — freezes, arbitrary minting, upgrades,\nrebases — lives in the listed token, not in the vault. Permissionless listing means the registry\nis a directory, not a whitelist, and the UI should say so.\n\n---\n\n## Build & test\n\n```\nforge build\nforge test\n```\n\n23 tests: claim accounting and pro-rata yield, rounding invariants (incl. a fuzz \"round trip never\nprofits\"), the inflation attack, fee-on-transfer rejection, reentrancy, and the factory's handling\nof `bytes32` metadata, missing metadata, undecodable metadata, non-contract assets, duplicate\nlistings and absurd decimals.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":484,"cache_read_input_tokens":71298,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":484},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f4bfc168-dec5-486a-8a3d-42ef222b540d","uuid":"34db02b9-d17e-4a3d-8070-0f74680ad9fb","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:35:11.788Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTnpgj5NKMgvPFVDo5H"}
