Its total holdings are read live:\n\n```\ntotalAssets() = asset.balanceOf(vault)\n```\n\nThere is no internal accounting counter. That is forced by the yield model — the keeper pushes\ntokens in with a plain `transfer` and never calls the vault, so there is no hook where a counter\ncould be bumped. Yield is, definitionally, the balance going up.\n\nShares are priced against that balance, with a **virtual offset** of `1` asset and `1e6` shares\nbaked into both directions:\n\n```\nconvertToShares(assets) = assets * (totalSupply + 1e6) / (totalAssets + 1)\nconvertToAssets(shares) = shares * (totalAssets + 1) / (totalSupply + 1e6)\n```\n\nA holder's claim is just `convertToAssets(balanceOf(holder))`, exposed as `maxWithdraw(holder)`.\nBecause the claim is a fraction of a live balance, a keeper transfer of `Y` raises every holder's\nclaim by `Y * (their share of supply)` in the same transaction, with nobody calling anything.\n\nShare token decimals are **asset decimals + 6**. A vault over USDC (6) has 12-decimal shares. Do\nnot assume they match — that offset is the inflation-attack mitigation, see below.\n\n### Worked example\n\n| Step | totalAssets | totalSupply | Alice's claim | Bob's claim |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Alice deposits 1,000 | 1,000 | 1e9 | 1,000 | — |\n| Bob deposits 3,000 | 4,000 | 4e9 | 1,000 | 3,000 |\n| Keeper transfers 400 | 4,400 | 4e9 | 1,100 | 3,300 |\n| Bob redeems all | 1,100 | 1e9 | 1,100 | 0 |\n\nBob's 3,300 includes his 300 of yield; Alice's claim is untouched by his exit.\n\n### Rounding\n\nEvery conversion rounds against the caller and in favour of the vault, so no sequence of\noperations can extract more than was put in (`testFuzz_roundTripNeverProfits`):\n\n| Operation | Rounds |\n| --- | --- |\n| `deposit` → shares minted | down |\n| `mint` → assets pulled | up |\n| `withdraw` → shares burned | up |\n| `redeem` → assets sent | down |\n\nConsequence: a deposit-and-immediately-exit round trip returns **at most** what went in, usually\n1 wei less. That is expected, not a bug.\n\nOperations that would round to zero **revert** (`ZeroShares` / `ZeroAssets`) rather than silently\ntransferring value for nothing. Dust deposits into a very high-priced vault therefore fail; they\ndo not get confiscated.\n\n### Why the virtual offset exists\n\nBecause `totalAssets()` is a live balance, anyone can move the share price by sending tokens in.\nThat is the feature (it's how yield works) and also the classic ERC-4626 inflation attack: be the\nfirst depositor with 1 wei, donate a pile, and the next depositor's shares round to zero.\n\nThe `1e6` virtual share offset bounds this. A donation attack can cost a victim **at most the\ndust below one whole share**, and to inflate the price far enough to matter the attacker has to\ndonate roughly `1e6 ×` what they could take — most of which the virtual shares absorb permanently.\n`test_inflationAttackIsUnprofitable` runs the attack: with a 500,000-token donation against a\n10,000-token depositor, the victim loses ~0.24 tokens and the attacker burns ~250,000.\n\nThe zero-share revert is the backstop for the extreme tail of the same attack.\n\n---\n\n## Listing a token\n\n`createVault(asset)` is open to anyone and takes only the asset address. The vault is built here\nfrom fixed bytecode, so a lister cannot inject parameters, and CREATE2-with-asset-as-salt means\nthere is exactly one vault per asset — a second call reverts.\n\n**`isVault(v) == true` means \"this vault runs our bytecode\". It says nothing about the token\nunderneath.** The factory does not and cannot vet assets. Before promoting a vault anywhere\nuser-facing, check these by hand:\n\n- **Address identity.** The share token's name/symbol are copied from the asset, and the asset\n  controls those strings. A scam clone whose `symbol()` returns `USDC` produces a perfectly real\n  `svUSDC` vault. Match the asset address against a list you trust; never match on symbol.\n- **Fee-on-transfer / deflationary.** Deposits revert with `UnexpectedAssetsReceived` — the vault\n  refuses to credit shares for tokens it did not receive, because doing so would dilute every\n  existing holder. The failure mode is safe but total: the vault is dead. Test a deposit before\n  listing. Also watch for tokens with a fee switch currently set to zero — they can turn it on\n  later and freeze deposits (existing holders can still withdraw).\n- **Blacklists / pausability** (USDC, USDT). The issuer can freeze the vault's balance, which\n  freezes withdrawals for everyone. Not fixable at the vault layer; it is a risk to disclose, not\n  to engineer around.\n- **Upgradeable proxies.** The token can change its rules after listing. Whatever you diligence\n  today is only true today.\n- **Rebasing tokens.** They work mechanically — a positive rebase reads as yield and lifts every\n  claim, which is the behaviour you want. A *negative* rebase reduces every claim pro-rata, with\n  no warning to depositors. Disclose or don't list.\n- **Transfer hooks (ERC-777 / ERC-1363).** All four entry points are `nonReentrant`, so a hook\n  cannot re-enter and read a half-updated share price. Still prefer plain tokens.\n- **Decimals.** Above 36 the listing reverts (share decimals would overflow `uint8`). Tokens whose\n  `decimals()` reverts are treated as 18 by ERC-4626 — fine, but check that the token really is\n  18, or the UI will misprice it.\n- **Seed the vault yourself.** Make the first deposit with a non-trivial amount and never withdraw\n  it. Virtual shares already make the inflation attack uneconomical; a real first deposit makes it\n  impossible and costs you nothing but the principal.\n\n---\n\n## Running the keeper\n\nThe keeper's whole job is `asset.transfer(vault, amount)`. Everything that can go wrong is\noperational:\n\n- **Use `transfer`, never `deposit`.** `deposit()` mints shares to the keeper — the keeper ends up\n  owning the yield instead of distributing it. A plain transfer is what lifts every holder's claim.\n- **Never send the wrong token, and never send to the wrong address.** There is no rescue\n  function. Assets other than the vault's own are permanently stuck; the vault's asset sent to the\n  wrong vault becomes a gift to that vault's depositors. Assert `token == vault.asset()` and\n  `factory.isVault(vault)` in the bot before every send.\n- **Skip vaults with `totalSupply() == 0`.** With no depositors there is nobody to lift; the\n  virtual shares absorb most of the transfer permanently and the rest becomes a windfall for\n  whoever deposits next.\n- **Send through a private relay / bundle.** See the accepted risk below — this is the one that\n  actually costs money if you get it wrong.\n- **Prefer frequent small transfers over rare large ones.** Same reason.\n- **Don't send dust.** A transfer that is small relative to `totalAssets` can round away to nothing\n  for individual holders. It won't revert; it just quietly does nothing for small positions.\n- **Handle non-standard ERC-20s in the bot.** The vault uses `SafeERC20` internally, but the\n  keeper's own transfer needs the same treatment (USDT returns no bool; approvals to non-zero\n  values revert).\n- **Monitor `totalAssets()` per vault.** Between keeper runs it should only move on deposits and\n  withdrawals. An unexplained drop means the asset did something — blacklist, negative rebase,\n  upgrade — and is the signal to stop listing it.\n\n---\n\n## Accepted risks\n\n**Yield sandwiching (the significant one).** Yield is recognised the instant it lands, and there is\nno lockup — both are stated product requirements, and together they mean a keeper transfer can be\nsandwiched. Someone watching the mempool deposits a large amount in the block before the transfer,\ntakes a pro-rata cut of yield they were never exposed to, and withdraws immediately after. With a\npublic transaction and a large enough attacker, most of a given yield distribution can be captured\nfrom real depositors.\n\nNothing in the contracts prevents this, so it is handled operationally: **send keeper transactions\nthrough a private relay, and distribute little and often.** That reduces it from a standing tax to\nan occasional leak.\n\nIf you'd rather close it in the contracts, the change is to vest each incoming transfer linearly\nover a period (`totalAssets()` returns `balance - unvestedYield`, à la xERC4626 / Yearn v3). It\nstays ERC-4626-compliant and depositors still have no lockup — but yield stops being instant,\nwhich contradicts \"the transfer lifts every holder's claim right away\", so I've left it out rather\nthan change the product's semantics unilaterally. Say the word and it's a small, self-contained\naddition to `SaveVault`.\n\n**Permanently stuck dust.** The virtual shares mean a small amount of the vault's balance is never\nclaimable, and a donation into a fully-emptied vault stays there for the next depositor. This is\nthe price of the inflation-attack mitigation and is bounded by roughly one share's worth.\n\n**The asset is the trust boundary.** Every remaining risk — freezes, arbitrary minting, upgrades,\nrebases — lives in the listed token, not in the vault. Permissionless listing means the registry\nis a directory, not a whitelist, and the UI should say so.\n\n---\n\n## Build & test\n\n```\nforge build\nforge test\n```\n\n23 tests: claim accounting and pro-rata yield, rounding invariants (incl. a fuzz \"round trip never\nprofits\"), the inflation attack, fee-on-transfer rejection, reentrancy, and the factory's handling\nof `bytes32` metadata, missing metadata, undecodable metadata, non-contract assets, duplicate\nlistings and absurd decimals.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

Dust deposits into a very high-priced vault therefore fail; they\ndo not get confiscated.\n\n### Why the virtual offset exists\n\nBecause `totalAssets()` is a live balance, anyone can move the share price by sending tokens in.\nThat is the feature (it's how yield works) and also the classic ERC-4626 inflation attack: be the\nfirst depositor with 1 wei, donate a pile, and the next depositor's shares round to zero.\n\nThe `1e6` virtual share offset bounds this. A donation attack can cost a victim **at most the\ndust below one whole share**, and to inflate the price far enough to matter the attacker has to\ndonate roughly `1e6 ×` what they could take — most of which the virtual shares absorb permanently.\n`test_inflationAttackIsUnprofitable` runs the attack: with a 500,000-token donation against a\n10,000-token depositor, the victim loses ~0.24 tokens and the attacker burns ~250,000.\n\nThe zero-share revert is the backstop for the extreme tail of the same attack.\n\n---\n\n## Listing a token\n\n`createVault(asset)` is open to anyone and takes only the asset address. The vault is built here\nfrom fixed bytecode, so a lister cannot inject parameters, and CREATE2-with-asset-as-salt means\nthere is exactly one vault per asset — a second call reverts.\n\n**`isVault(v) == true` means \"this vault runs our bytecode\". It says nothing about the token\nunderneath.** The factory does not and cannot vet assets. Before promoting a vault anywhere\nuser-facing, check these by hand:\n\n- **Address identity.** The share token's name/symbol are copied from the asset, and the asset\n  controls those strings. A scam clone whose `symbol()` returns `USDC` produces a perfectly real\n  `svUSDC` vault. Match the asset address against a list you trust; never match on symbol.\n- **Fee-on-transfer / deflationary.** Deposits revert with `UnexpectedAssetsReceived` — the vault\n  refuses to credit shares for tokens it did not receive, because doing so would dilute every\n  existing holder. The failure mode is safe but total: the vault is dead. Test a deposit before\n  listing. Also watch for tokens with a fee switch currently set to zero — they can turn it on\n  later and freeze deposits (existing holders can still withdraw).\n- **Blacklists / pausability** (USDC, USDT). The issuer can freeze the vault's balance, which\n  freezes withdrawals for everyone. Not fixable at the vault layer; it is a risk to disclose, not\n  to engineer around.\n- **Upgradeable proxies.** The token can change its rules after listing. Whatever you diligence\n  today is only true today.\n- **Rebasing tokens.** They work mechanically — a positive rebase reads as yield and lifts every\n  claim, which is the behaviour you want. A *negative* rebase reduces every claim pro-rata, with\n  no warning to depositors. Disclose or don't list.\n- **Transfer hooks (ERC-777 / ERC-1363).** All four entry points are `nonReentrant`, so a hook\n  cannot re-enter and read a half-updated share price. Still prefer plain tokens.\n- **Decimals.** Above 36 the listing reverts (share decimals would overflow `uint8`). Tokens whose\n  `decimals()` reverts are treated as 18 by ERC-4626 — fine, but check that the token really is\n  18, or the UI will misprice it.\n- **Seed the vault yourself.** Make the first deposit with a non-trivial amount and never withdraw\n  it. Virtual shares already make the inflation attack uneconomical; a real first deposit makes it\n  impossible and costs you nothing but the principal.\n\n---\n\n## Running the keeper\n\nThe keeper's whole job is `asset.transfer(vault, amount)`. Everything that can go wrong is\noperational:\n\n- **Use `transfer`, never `deposit`.** `deposit()` mints shares to the keeper — the keeper ends up\n  owning the yield instead of distributing it. A plain transfer is what lifts every holder's claim.\n- **Never send the wrong token, and never send to the wrong address.** There is no rescue\n  function. Assets other than the vault's own are permanently stuck; the vault's asset sent to the\n  wrong vault becomes a gift to that vault's depositors. Assert `token == vault.asset()` and\n  `factory.isVault(vault)` in the bot before every send.\n- **Skip vaults with `totalSupply() == 0`.** With no depositors there is nobody to lift; the\n  virtual shares absorb most of the transfer permanently and the rest becomes a windfall for\n  whoever deposits next.\n- **Send through a private relay / bundle.** See the accepted risk below — this is the one that\n  actually costs money if you get it wrong.\n- **Prefer frequent small transfers over rare large ones.** Same reason.\n- **Don't send dust.** A transfer that is small relative to `totalAssets` can round away to nothing\n  for individual holders. It won't revert; it just quietly does nothing for small positions.\n- **Handle non-standard ERC-20s in the bot.** The vault uses `SafeERC20` internally, but the\n  keeper's own transfer needs the same treatment (USDT returns no bool; approvals to non-zero\n  values revert).\n- **Monitor `totalAssets()` per vault.** Between keeper runs it should only move on deposits and\n  withdrawals. An unexplained drop means the asset did something — blacklist, negative rebase,\n  upgrade — and is the signal to stop listing it.\n\n---\n\n## Accepted risks\n\n**Yield sandwiching (the significant one).** Yield is recognised the instant it lands, and there is\nno lockup — both are stated product requirements, and together they mean a keeper transfer can be\nsandwiched. Someone watching the mempool deposits a large amount in the block before the transfer,\ntakes a pro-rata cut of yield they were never exposed to, and withdraws immediately after. With a\npublic transaction and a large enough attacker, most of a given yield distribution can be captured\nfrom real depositors.\n\nNothing in the contracts prevents this, so it is handled operationally: **send keeper transactions\nthrough a private relay, and distribute little and often.** That reduces it from a standing tax to\nan occasional leak.\n\nIf you'd rather close it in the contracts, the change is to vest each incoming transfer linearly\nover a period (`totalAssets()` returns `balance - unvestedYield`, à la xERC4626 / Yearn v3). It\nstays ERC-4626-compliant and depositors still have no lockup — but yield stops being instant,\nwhich contradicts \"the transfer lifts every holder's claim right away\", so I've left it out rather\nthan change the product's semantics unilaterally. Say the word and it's a small, self-contained\naddition to `SaveVault`.\n\n**Permanently stuck dust.** The virtual shares mean a small amount of the vault's balance is never\nclaimable, and a donation into a fully-emptied vault stays there for the next depositor. This is\nthe price of the inflation-attack mitigation and is bounded by roughly one share's worth.\n\n**The asset is the trust boundary.** Every remaining risk — freezes, arbitrary minting, upgrades,\nrebases — lives in the listed token, not in the vault. Permissionless listing means the registry\nis a directory, not a whitelist, and the UI should say so.\n\n---\n\n## Build & test\n\n```\nforge build\nforge test\n```\n\n23 tests: claim accounting and pro-rata yield, rounding invariants (incl. a fuzz \"round trip never\nprofits\"), the inflation attack, fee-on-transfer rejection, reentrancy, and the factory's handling\nof `bytes32` metadata, missing metadata, undecodable metadata, non-contract assets, duplicate\nlistings and absurd decimals.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":44,"oldLines":6,"newStart":44,"newLines":9,"lines":[" "," ### Worked example"," ","+Whole-token units, an 18-decimal asset, figures rounded (the virtual offset moves digits far below","+what's shown):","+"," | Step | totalAssets | totalSupply | Alice's claim | Bob's claim |"," | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |"," | Alice deposits 1,000 | 1,000 | 1e9 | 1,000 | — |"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTyG4F3YVYLKgN6ch87","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. `forge build` clean, `forge test` 23/23 passing.\n\n## What's there\n\n```\nsrc/SaveVault.sol          ERC-4626 vault; share token = the transferable receipt\nsrc/SaveVaultFactory.sol   permissionless registry, one canonical vault per ERC-20\nscript/DeployFactory.s.sol the only thing we deploy\ntest/                      23 tests + hostile-token mocks\nNOTES.md                   claim math + operator checklists\n```\n\nVaults are **ownerless** — no pause, upgrade, fee switch, or rescue function. A rescue helper would double as an admin drain since the vault's asset is just a balance.\n\n## Design points worth your attention\n\n**`totalAssets()` is the live balance,** which the yield model forces (the keeper never calls the vault, so nothing can bump a counter). That makes the share price donation-sensitive — the classic ERC-4626 inflation attack. Mitigated with a `1e6` virtual-share offset plus a revert on zero-share/zero-asset operations. `test_inflationAttackIsUnprofitable` runs it: a 500k-token donation against a 10k depositor costs the victim 0.245 tokens and burns 249,999 of the attacker's.\n\n**Fee-on-transfer assets are rejected, not half-supported.** Deposits check the balance delta and revert if the vault didn't receive exactly what it asked for — crediting shares for tokens that never arrived dilutes every existing holder. Product consequence: someone *will* list a FoT token permissionlessly, and its vault will be permanently dead rather than quietly lossy. That's the failure mode I picked; flag it if you'd rather support them via delta-credited shares.\n\n**Two things I'd want you to decide on:**\n\n1. **Yield sandwiching.** Instant recognition + no lockup are both stated requirements, and together they mean a public keeper transfer is sandwichable — deposit big in the block before, withdraw after. Nothing in the contracts stops it, so NOTES.md handles it operationally (private relay, little and often). The contract-level fix is linear vesting of each incoming transfer (`totalAssets = balance - unvestedYield`, xERC4626-style) — still ERC-4626, still no lockup, but yield stops being instant, which contradicts your description. I left it out rather than change product semantics on my own; it's a small self-contained addition if you want it.\n\n2. **`isVault()` proves bytecode, not identity.** Name/symbol are copied from the asset, so an impostor whose `symbol()` returns `USDC` yields a genuine `svUSDC` vault. The UI has to match on address and say \"listing ≠ endorsement.\"\n\nThe factory treats the asset as hostile on read: `bytes32` metadata (MKR), reverting metadata, undecodable ABI, oversized strings, EOAs, duplicates, and `decimals() > 36` (would overflow the share token's `decimals()`) are all handled or rejected up front. All four entry points are `nonReentrant` since hooked tokens can be listed."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":258,"cache_read_input_tokens":88616,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":258},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f4bfc168-dec5-486a-8a3d-42ef222b540d","uuid":"669e81cf-bfdc-40a8-8519-303b24786d31","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:36:32.955Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTyEmrD2SV4Y7sg4DGw"}
